CEO and executive team

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Launch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a Pro plan at $12 more per seat, not as a $149 add-on, and plan on about $2.9M of ARR, not $8M
Copilot creates real value, but less than the internal case claims
–	Beta productivity rose 11% against 2% for matched accounts, among volunteers
–	AI costs at most $642K of new ARR a year in Routewise deals
As a $149 add-on, Copilot would sell to one account in seven and earn least on heavy users
–	Only 14% paid when asked, against 46% in the survey
–	That gives about $2.5M of ARR, under a third of the $8M case
A Pro plan at $12 more per seat earns more, keeps margin and closes the NRR gap
–	If 33% move up, as in 2023, Pro adds 5 percentage points of NRR
–	A usage allowance keeps company gross margin at 76.5%
A Q2 launch costs two more quarters of mobile churn, worth paying unless the rewrite fixes most of it
–	Mobile reliability drives 4.5 times as much churn as AI features
–	Copilot first wins unless the rewrite removes over half of mobile churn
Launch on four conditions: a tested gain, a usage allowance, 26% Pro uptake and an early mobile restart
